code_label: Shallow initial distributions improve qGAN learning
text_span: we propose a novel method for generating an initial distribution that improves the learning eﬃciency of qGANs
rationale: States the paper’s main objective and claimed contribution.

code_label: Classical label replacement generates distributions
text_span: Our method uses the classical process of label replacement to generate various probability distributions in shallow quantum circuits.
rationale: Summarizes the central methodological idea.

code_label: Target distributions demonstrated
text_span: we demonstrate that our proposed method can generate the log-normal distribution, which is pivotal in ﬁnancial engineering, as well as the triangular distribution and the bimodal distribution
rationale: Identifies the distributions used to validate the method.

code_label: Initial distribution linked to initial weights
text_span: the initial distribution proposed in our research is related to the problem of determining the initial weights for qGANs
rationale: Highlights an analytical observation connecting initialization and weights.

code_label: Quantum expectation estimation motivates loading distributions
text_span: Executing the quantum expectation estimation algorithm needs the construction of a quantum circuit capable of loading a probability distribution into a quantum state.
rationale: Explains the application context motivating the work.

code_label: Grover-Rudolph is too deep for NISQ
text_span: it requires up to O(2n) gates and quantum circuit depth, making it diﬃcult to use in NISQ devices.
rationale: States a limitation of the prior state-preparation approach.

code_label: Normal initial distribution may lose shallow-circuit advantage
text_span: using the normal distribution requires more depth of the quantum circuit.
rationale: Identifies the depth cost of the previously suggested initialization.

code_label: Label replacement avoids extra quantum gates
text_span: label replacement can be implemented by a classical process because it transforms a random variable that determines what value corresponds to the output of a measurement result.
rationale: Explains why the proposed method is implementable without deeper quantum circuits.

code_label: Depth-one implementation of initial distribution
text_span: The circuit Init for generating the distribution before the replacement of Figure 4a can be implemented with a gate of depth d = 1
rationale: Specifies the shallow circuit depth of the proposed initialization.

code_label: Knowledge-reflecting initialization procedure
text_span: we first sort the target probability distribution in order of increasing probability.
rationale: Captures a key step in the fitting algorithm.

code_label: Recursive angle fitting from probability mass
text_span: We repeat the above procedure to determine the angle of Ry.
rationale: Describes the iterative construction of the initialization angles.

code_label: Largest target probability is matched
text_span: we can always generate an initial distribution such that the largest probability in the target probability distribution coincides with the largest probability in the probability distribution created by label replacement.
rationale: States a structural property of the constructed initial distribution.

code_label: Simulation compared three initializations
text_span: the initial distribution was our initial distribution, the uniform distribution, and the normal distribution with a mean and standard deviation of the target probability distribution.
rationale: Identifies the experimental comparison set.

code_label: Training protocol and optimizer choices
text_span: The AMSGRAD [16] was used for training, with a learning rate of lr = 10−4 and coeﬃcients for calculating moments of a gradient of β1 = 0.7 and β2 = 0.99.
rationale: Records the optimization setup used in simulation.

code_label: Relative entropy used as evaluation metric
text_span: We use relative entropy to measures to evaluate the training performance.
rationale: States the metric used to assess results.

code_label: Log-normal parameters and initialization angles
text_span: the parameters of our initial distribution are θlognormal = [0.36π, 0.40π, 0.44π]
rationale: Provides the concrete initialization used for one target distribution.

code_label: Triangular parameters and initialization angles
text_span: θtriangular = [0.29π, 0.43π, 0.48π]
rationale: Provides the concrete initialization used for the triangular case.

code_label: Bimodal parameters and initialization angles
rationale: Provides the concrete initialization used for the bimodal case.

code_label: Permutation of measurement outcomes is specified
text_span: the permutation of each measurement outcome is
rationale: Introduces the label-replacement mappings used in experiments.

code_label: Our method beats uniform initialization
text_span: our method is superior to the uniform distribution as initial distribution in both mean and minimum values of relative entropy
rationale: Summarizes the main comparative result against the uniform baseline.

code_label: Normal initialization remains stronger for some cases
text_span: our method is inferior in the mean value of relative entropy but equally suitable for the minimum value compared to the case where the normal distribution is an initial distribution.
rationale: Reports a nuanced comparison with the normal baseline.

code_label: Log-normal case favors proposed method over normal
text_span: when the log-normal distribution is the target distribution, our method outperforms the normal distribution as the initial distribution in both mean and minimum values
rationale: Highlights the strongest reported advantage of the proposed method.

code_label: NISQ advantage from avoiding two-qubit gates
text_span: the normal distribution requires two-qubit gates, which is expensive due to the high noise content in NISQ devices
rationale: Connects the result to hardware constraints and noise considerations.

code_label: Robustness to qubit scaling
text_span: our method is always “d = 1”, whereas normal distributions may lose the advantage of circuit generation using qGANs if the quantum circuit making the normal distribution is deeper for more than four qubits.
rationale: States a scalability advantage of the proposed initialization.

code_label: Initial distribution equals initial weights
text_span: our initial distribution can be understood as the initial weights of the quantum generators
rationale: Makes the conceptual link between initialization and generator parameters explicit.

code_label: Hadamard and Ry are equivalent on |0⟩
text_span: these two operations are the same for the initial state |0⟩.
rationale: Supports the claim that uniform initialization can be absorbed into weights.

code_label: Proposed and uniform initializations can be depth zero
text_span: our initial distribution, as well as uniform distributions, can be implemented at depth d = 0.
rationale: Summarizes the depth interpretation of the initialization schemes.

code_label: Future work on broader distributions
text_span: Our future works are to examine whether this method maintains its eﬃcacy for probability distributions beyond the log-normal, triangular, and bimodal distributions.
rationale: States a planned extension beyond the tested distributions.

code_label: Future work on larger qubit counts
text_span: We also intend to assess its performance as the number of qubits increases.
rationale: Identifies a planned scalability study.

code_label: Future work on measurements and parameters
text_span: it is also necessary to evaluate the impact of the number of measurements and the number of parameters (weights) on accuracy.
rationale: Notes another planned analysis affecting accuracy.

code_label: Code not publicly available
text_span: The underlying code for this study is not publicly available
rationale: States an availability limitation relevant to reproducibility.
